chief_complaint.quote: I think I gave her too much Tylenol. I mixed up the bottles.
chief_complaint.explanation: Documents the problem prompting the call.

assessment.text: Five milliliters of infant Tylenol drops was given about twenty minutes earlier.
assessment.speaker: Caller
assessment.quote: And I gave her five milliliters. A full five.

assessment.text: The infant drops bottle said eighty milligrams per point eight milliliter.
assessment.speaker: Caller
assessment.quote: It says eighty milligrams per point eight milliliter.

assessment.text: She was fussy and teething.
assessment.speaker: Caller
assessment.quote: She's been fussy since midnight. It's the teeth.

assessment.text: She had no vomiting or unusual sleepiness.
assessment.speaker: Caller
assessment.quote: No. No vomiting. She's alert.

response.text: Advised calling poison control and going to the emergency room now.
response.speaker: Nurse
response.quote: call poison control now.

response.text: Planned to page the on-call clinician.
response.speaker: Nurse
response.quote: I'm going to page the on-call clinician right now

response.text: Planned to call back within fifteen minutes.
response.speaker: Nurse
response.quote: I'll call you back within fifteen minutes

education.text: Advised giving no more acetaminophen tonight, calling poison control, and bringing both bottles and the syringe to the emergency room.
education.speaker: Nurse
education.quote: don't give her any more acetaminophen

education.text: Advised keeping only one concentration in the house, writing the dose on the bottle, and using the bottle's own syringe.
education.speaker: Nurse
education.quote: Keep only one concentration in the house.

call poison control now.
